source: etherscan.io/accounts/label/<slug> and etherscan.io/labelcloud, verified by direct fetch 2026-09-23
note: Not exhaustive. Verified, primary-source addresses only -- nothing copied from a secondary dataset without checking against Etherscan directly (see docs/DATA-SOURCES.md for why eth-labels was rejected as a primary source).

wallets.label: Coinbase 10
wallets.note: found via our own live scan (an $8.3M USDC transfer), not a research search -- confirmed against Etherscan directly. This is the intended feedback loop: real observed data drives which addresses get identified next.

kraken.structure: the direct label page (/accounts/label/kraken) returns thousands of per-user 'Kraken Dep: 0x...' deposit addresses, NOT a small main-wallet set -- but the actual main custody/hot wallets DO exist under different individual labels, found via general web search instead of the label page. This confirms the general on-chain-analytics pattern: per-user deposit addresses eventually sweep funds into a small set of real custody wallets; watch those, not the deposit addresses.

wallets.label: Kraken: Hot Wallet
wallets.note: balance verified near-zero at check time -- expected for an active hot wallet, always fetch live balance, never trust a cached figure from search results

wallets.label: Kraken 3

entities.label: Abraxas Capital Management: Heka Funds
entities.note: moved $25-32M in USDT/USDC across several observed transfers, appears in a chain with two other addresses (0xa188eec8..., 0xee7ae85f...) that are likely related wallets of the same entity, not yet individually confirmed

excluded_or_deferred.okx: Label cloud only showed an 'okx-labs' entry (11 accounts) -- does not look like their main exchange wallets. Not verified, not included.
excluded_or_deferred.bybit: Label cloud only showed a 'bybit-exploit' entry (77 accounts) -- appears to be hack-incident-related addresses, not their main exchange wallets. Not verified, not included.

known_false_positive_traps: Substring-matching 'binance' (or any exchange name) against a label/nameTag field catches OTHER platforms' individual deposit wallets INTO that exchange (e.g. 'Bilaxy: Binance Dep: 0x...', 'Alameda Research: Binance Deposit') -- these are not the exchange's own wallets. This is how the eth-labels dataset's 5102 'binance' matches were almost entirely false positives. Always verify against the exchange's own primary label page, not a substring match.
'0x: Coinbase Wallet Proxy' is a 0x-protocol smart contract, unrelated to Coinbase the company -- a naming coincidence, not a Coinbase wallet.

A search result's stated wallet balance can be badly stale (Kraken 3 was quoted at 801,052 ETH in one search snippet; the live Etherscan value was 0.057 ETH). Balances are not durable facts -- only addresses/labels are worth recording here; always fetch balances live at run time.

A wallet's own dedicated Etherscan label page (/accounts/label/<name>) is not always the right list for a given exchange -- Kraken's page returns per-user deposit addresses, not the main custody wallets, which had to be found via general search instead.
